label: 500 BC
title: The Persian Empire & the Greek world
summary: Darius I rules the Achaemenid Empire from the Aegean to the Indus, linked by the Royal Road. Greek and Phoenician city-states have colonised the Mediterranean and Black Sea coasts, Carthage dominates the western seas, and Rome is a young republic (traditionally founded 509 BC). The Ionian Revolt against Persia is about to break out (499 BC).

label: 0 CE
title: The Roman Empire under Augustus
summary: Around the turn of the era (there is no year zero — 1 BC is followed by AD 1) Augustus rules a Mediterranean that is, for the first time, under a single power. Roman roads and the grain fleets tie the provinces to Rome; Parthia rules Mesopotamia and Iran, and Nabataean caravans bring incense from Arabia to Gaza.

label: 300 CE
title: The Tetrarchy of Diocletian
summary: After the 3rd-century crisis, Diocletian has split power among four emperors, each ruling from a frontier capital: Nicomedia, Mediolanum, Sirmium and Thessalonica, and Augusta Treverorum. The frontiers hold again from Hadrian's Wall to the Euphrates, and the Peace of Nisibis (299) has pushed Rome beyond the Tigris. Christianity is spreading fast; the Great Persecution will begin in 303, and Constantine will found Constantinople in 330.

label: 500 CE
title: Successor kingdoms & the Eastern Roman Empire
summary: The western empire has given way to Germanic kingdoms: Theoderic the Ostrogoth rules Italy from Ravenna, the Vandals hold Carthage, the Visigoths Toulouse and Spain. Emperor Anastasius I governs the East from Constantinople, fed by the Egyptian grain fleet, while the Sasanian Persians rule from Ctesiphon. Pilgrims travel the roads to Jerusalem.

label: 565 CE
title: The age of Justinian — only the Eastern Romans remain
summary: The western empire is long gone, but Justinian (died 14 November 565) has won back Africa from the Vandals (533–534), Italy from the Ostrogoths (535–554) and a strip of southern Spain, making the Mediterranean briefly a Roman lake again. Hagia Sophia (537) crowns Constantinople, though plague (541) has ravaged the empire. Frankish kings rule Gaul, the Visigoths rule Spain from Toledo, and Khosrow I rules Persia. The Lombards wait in Pannonia; they will invade Italy in 568.
